text: 62-year-old male. DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Penis and Digit (likely arising from chronic mucocutaneous leishmaniasis or chronic inflammatory changes given the African origin and prior misdiagnoses), complicated by heavy tobacco use. The histopathology showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures in a non-healing, crusted lesion is diagnostic of malignancy. Given the dual presentation (penis and digit) in a high-risk demographic with prior syphilis treatment failure, further imaging for metastatic workup is indicated.
